- [USER] User expressed interest in The Orioles and their notable performances or collaborations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Orioles are credited with creating the R&B sound that helped shape early rock and roll.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Notable performances and collaborations of The Orioles include:
  1. "It's Too Soon to Know" (1951) - Their biggest hit, which reached #1 on the R&B charts.
  2. Collaboration with Sonny Til - Recorded songs including "Crying in the Chapel" and "In the Mission of St. Augustine".
  3. "Tell Me So" (1952) - A popular song later covered by The Moonglows and The Duprees.
  4. Collaboration with Johnny Reed - Recorded "It's a Cold, Cold World" which reached #4 on the R&B charts in 1953.
  5. "What Are You Doing New Year's Eve?" (1949) - A holiday classic covered by many artists.
  6. "Lonely Christmas" (1953) - A seasonal hit with a spoken-word intro and a somber melody.
  7. Collaboration with Charlie Barnet - Recorded "Until the Real Thing Comes Along" in 1955.
  8. "Crying in the Chapel" (1953) - A gospel-tinged tune that became a hit for Elvis Presley in 1965.
  9. Collaboration with Big Maybelle - Recorded "Rain Down Rain" in 1954.
  10. "Baby, Please Don't Go" (1952) - An uptempo song featuring lively vocal delivery and jazzy solos.
